title: Wait for the Database
story:
[RADIO -- PETREL, CHANNEL 9]

Rafael Duarte: Kestrel Point, Petrel. I sail at dawn and my cargo manifest has to be in your database before I load. Last time the migration ran while Postgres was still starting, the table never got made, and I loaded half the crates blind. Over.

Ingrid, from the doorway: Compose project `manifest`, engineer. Service `db` is Postgres, container name `manifest-db`, with a health check. Service `migrate` runs `migrations/001_cargo.sql` once the database is healthy, then exits cleanly. The tide won't wait. Over.
objectives: Service `db` runs `postgres:16-alpine` with `container_name: manifest-db`, a `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, and a healthcheck
Service `migrate` runs `psql` against host `db` with the file `/migrations/001_cargo.sql` (mount `./migrations`), starts only when `db` is healthy and exits with code 0
Bring the project up: `manifest-db` is healthy and table `cargo_manifest` contains 3 rows
startingState: `/workspace/migrations/001_cargo.sql` creates and fills `cargo_manifest`; there is no compose file yet.
hints: A container being 'started' is not the same as the service inside it being ready. Compose can wait for a health check: give `db` a `healthcheck`, and make `migrate` depend on it with a condition rather than just a name.

Use `pg_isready` as the health test and `depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy` on the migrator. The migrator can reuse the Postgres image just for its `psql` client; give it `PGPASSWORD` and set `restart: "no"` so it exits once and stays done. Use `-h 127.0.0.1` in the health test so it only turns healthy when Postgres accepts network connections.

A complete file, followed by `docker compose up -d`:

```yaml
name: manifest
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: manifest-db
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: kestrel-pass
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  migrate:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      PGPASSWORD: kestrel-pass
    volumes:
      - ./migrations:/migrations:ro
    command: ["psql", "-h", "db", "-U", "postgres", "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-f", "/migrations/001_cargo.sql"]
    restart: "no"
```

validation.description: The one-shot `migrate` container finished with exit code 0

solution:
cat > compose.yaml <<'EOF'
name: manifest
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: manifest-db
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: kestrel-pass
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  migrate:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      PGPASSWORD: kestrel-pass
    volumes:
      - ./migrations:/migrations:ro
    command: ["psql", "-h", "db", "-U", "postgres", "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-f", "/migrations/001_cargo.sql"]
    restart: "no"
EOF
debrief: `condition: service_healthy` makes the migrator wait for the moment the database actually answers, not just the moment its process starts. Pro tip: write migrations with `IF NOT EXISTS`, so rerunning the one-shot service is harmless.
